 Hiring founding engineers to build the future of how accounting work gets done.
 



  





 Reshaping an industry takes hard work. We're looking for high\-agency engineers who combine technical excellence, strong product taste, and a deep appetite to delight customers.

 Combinely is building an AI coworker for accountants.
 



  





 Accounting firms spend $180 billion on labor in the US alone while their workforce is shrinking – 75% of CPAs will retire in the next decade. Combinely bridges the gap with an AI coworker that uses the same tools and knowledge to produce client\-ready work just like a seasoned accountant.
 



  





 Built by an ex\-Google/Deloitte team, we're growing fast, backed by top investors, and already live inside leading accounting firms across the world.
 



  





**What you'll do** 



* Deliver magic – design, build, and ship agentic AI systems that can reason, use tools, and solve complex accounting tasks reliably.
* Work with customers – talk to users, sit with customers, understand what matters, and turn messy real\-world problems into a delightful product.

* Ambitious: you want to work hard on a hard problem, and you're excited by the pace of an early\-stage startup.
* Customer\-obsessed: user problems energise you, and you measure success in real\-world impact.
* High agency: you default to action, break through blockers, and leave things better than you found them.
* Product\-minded: you have strong taste, notice details others miss, and care about building something customers genuinely love.
* Growth\-oriented: you're excited to wade into the deep end, learn fast, and take ownership beyond your job title.

* Experience building and shipping LLM\-powered products.
* Use tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor intensely.
* Excited to work directly with customers, not just through tickets or product specs.
* Willing to travel to customer sites when needed.
* Excited to work in\-person with us 5 days a week.
* Authorised to work in the US.



  





**Interview process** 




 We aim to move fast and give an answer within 24 hours after each stage. You can expect an offer within 2 weeks from application.
 


1. Founder call, 30 mins – get to know each other and make sure we're on the same page.
2. Take\-home task, 72h – a realistic task you might take on at Combinely.
3. On\-site interview, 2–3h – deep\-dive on your take\-home, extend it with a new feature, walk through past projects, and have an open culture chat.



  





**Why join now** 



* Own meaningful equity – enough to not need another job if we succeed.
* Mentorship \+ autonomy – work shoulder\-to\-shoulder with the founders, not through layers of management.
* Impact – solve hard problems, influence product strategy, and reshape an entire industry.

Convoy Health is an AlleyCorp company — built inside the studio Kevin Ryan founded (MongoDB, Pearl Health). AlleyCorp was recently the most active early\-stage healthcare investor in the U.S., and it builds serious applied AI — Rogo (the Gen AI now used inside 25\+ banks and hedge funds) and Radical AI (its largest\-ever incubation). We're an early\-stage healthcare\-AI company putting agents and applied ML to work on the financial and operational decisions that run health systems, ACOs, and payers. Real customers, real data, in production today.
 



  





**The role** 




 You're our founding AI engineer — the person who owns the intelligence layer of the product. You'll design and ship the agentic systems that read our healthcare data, reason over it, call tools, and put decisions in front of finance and operations leaders: LLM orchestration, retrieval, tool\-use contracts, evals, guardrails, and the inference stack. You'll also own the data foundation that makes the AI trustworthy — the messy, high\-stakes healthcare data (claims, clinical, RCM) the models run on. No inherited stack, no playbook. A direct line to the CTO and your fingerprints on every decision that matters.
 



  





**Who you are** 
 — a bar on talent and trajectory, not a checklist of tools
 



 • You've shipped real AI in production — LLM\-powered, agentic, tool\-using systems serving real users. You've hit the hard parts (evals, latency, reliability, hallucination, cost) and shipped anyway.
 



 • You've been a founding or early engineer at a startup — or an exceptional engineer at a top company itching to build from zero. You move fast and own outcomes end to end.
 



 • You're fluent with data, and you've worked with messy, regulated, high\-stakes data. Healthcare claims (837/835/834\), clinical, or RCM experience is a real requirement here — you own the data foundation as well as the AI, and the AI is only as good as the data under it.
 



 • You're US\-based and authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship, now or in the future.
 



  





**What matters less than you'd think** 




 • The exact tools on your résumé. Our stack is modern (Python, modern LLM/agent frameworks, a cloud warehouse, dbt, Postgres), but we'd rather hire a brilliant builder who'll master ours than someone who's memorized a specific one.
 



 • Years of experience as a number. We've watched 5\-year builders out\-build 15\-year veterans. We index on slope, not tenure.
 



 • A traditional enterprise path. If you're happiest tuning a mature system inside a big org, this isn't it — this is a 0\-to\-1 seat.
 



  





**Why this seat is rare** 




 • "Founding" is usually just a title. Here it's the job — you're the first AI hire, you define how an entire healthcare\-AI company uses AI, and you report straight to the CTO.
 



 • The backing is real. AlleyCorp doesn't just write checks; it builds category leaders from zero — MongoDB, Pearl Health, Rogo — and holds its AI to a "real work, not copilots" bar. You get a rocketship's backing with a garage's ownership.
 



 • You build real AI, not a copilot demo. Live customers and production healthcare data from day one — you ship into real workflows instead of waiting on a dataset.
 



 • The upside matches the bet: meaningful founding\-level equity, behind a backer whose last data company is worth tens of billions.
